question.:question/problem:
Evaluate
$$
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r,
$$
where $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=y\,\mathbf i+z\,\mathbf j+x\,\mathbf k$ and $C$ is the path
$$
\mathbf r(t)=t\,\mathbf i+t^2\,\mathbf j+t^3\,\mathbf k,\qquad 0\le t\le1.
$$
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use
$$
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=\int_0^1\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)\,\mathrm dt.
$$
Along the curve, $x=t$, $y=t^2$, and $z=t^3$. Hence
$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))=t^2\,\mathbf i+t^3\,\mathbf j+t\,\mathbf k.
$$
Differentiating the curve gives
$$
\mathbf r'(t)=\mathbf i+2t\,\mathbf j+3t^2\,\mathbf k.
$$
Match corresponding vector components in the dot product:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)&=t^2\cdot1+t^3\cdot2t+t\cdot3t^2\\
&=t^2+2t^4+3t^3.
\end{aligned}
$$
Thus
$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=\int_0^1(t^2+2t^4+3t^3)\,\mathrm dt\\
&=\left[\frac{t^3}{3}+\frac{2t^5}{5}+\frac{3t^4}{4}\right]_0^1\\
&=\frac13+\frac25+\frac34=\frac{89}{60}.
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate
$$
\int_C \mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r,
$$
where $\mathbf F(x,y,z)=x\,\mathbf i+z\,\mathbf j+y\,\mathbf k$ and
$$
\mathbf r(t)=t\,\mathbf i+2t\,\mathbf j+(1-t)\,\mathbf k,\qquad 0\le t\le1.
$$
*Hint: Use $\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=\int_0^1\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)\,\mathrm dt$ with $\mathbf r'(t)=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-\mathbf k$.*
question.:question/worked-solution:
Use the parametrized line-integral formula:
$$
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r=\int_0^1\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)\,\mathrm dt.
$$
Along the curve, $x=t$, $y=2t$, and $z=1-t$. Substitute these coordinates into the corresponding field components:
$$
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))=t\,\mathbf i+(1-t)\,\mathbf j+2t\,\mathbf k.
$$
Differentiate the curve component by component:
$$
\mathbf r'(t)=\mathbf i+2\mathbf j-\mathbf k.
$$
The dot product includes the negative third component:
$$
\begin{aligned}
\mathbf F(\mathbf r(t))\cdot\mathbf r'(t)&=t\cdot1+(1-t)\cdot2+2t\cdot(-1)\\
&=2-3t.
\end{aligned}
$$
Finally,
$$
\begin{aligned}
\int_C\mathbf F\cdot\mathrm d\mathbf r&=\int_0^1(2-3t)\,\mathrm dt\\
&=\left[2t-\frac32t^2\right]_0^1\\
&=2-\frac32=\frac12.
\end{aligned}
$$

question.:question/problem:
Evaluate ${\int}_{C}F\cdot\text{d}r$ given that $F(x,y)=(2 y - 1)\,i+(2 x - y + 1)\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=(- 2 t - 2)\,i+(- t - 1)\,j$ for $t\in[0,1].$

*Hint:* Use $\int_C F\cdot\mathrm d r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\mathrm dt$.
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=- 2 t - 2,\quad y=- t - 1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t)) \\ \begin{aligned} &=(2 y - 1)\,i+(2 x - y + 1)\,j \\ &=\begin{aligned}&\left(2 \left(- t - 1\right) - 1\right)\,i \\ &{} +\left(2 \left(- 2 t - 2\right) - \left(- t - 1\right) + 1\right)\,j\end{aligned} \\ &=(- 2 t - 3)\,i+(- 3 t - 2)\,j\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- 2 t - 2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(- t - 1)\,j \\  & =(-2)\,i+(-1)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&\left({(- 2 t - 3)\,i+(- 3 t - 2)\,j}\right) \\ &{} \cdot\left({(-2)\,i+(-1)\,j}\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(- 2 t - 3)\cdot(-2)+(- 3 t - 2) \\ &{} \cdot(-1)\end{aligned} \\ &=\left({4 t + 6}\right)+\left({3 t + 2}\right) \\ &=7 t + 8\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{gathered}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r \\ \begin{aligned} &=\int_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\int_{0}^{1}\left({7 t + 8}\right)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\left[{\frac{7 t^{2}}{2} + 8 t}\right]_{0}^{1} \\ &=((8)+\left(\frac{7}{2}\right))-((0)+(0)) \\ &=\left(\frac{23}{2}\right)-(0) \\ &=\frac{23}{2}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

$$
\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t + 2,\quad y=2 t + 1.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}F(r(t)) & =(- y)\,i+(- x - 2)\,j \\  & =\left(- \left(2 t + 1\right)\right)\,i+\left(- \left(t + 2\right) - 2\right)\,j \\  & =(- 2 t - 1)\,i+(- t - 4)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}r^{\prime}(t) & =\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\  & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t + 2)\,i+\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(2 t + 1)\,j \\  & =(1)\,i+(2)\,j\end{aligned}
$$

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&\left({(- 2 t - 1)\,i+(- t - 4)\,j}\right) \\ &{} \cdot\left({(1)\,i+(2)\,j}\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=(- 2 t - 1)\cdot(1)+(- t - 4)\cdot(2) \\ &=\left({- 2 t - 1}\right)+\left({- 2 t - 8}\right) \\ &=- 4 t - 9\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{gathered}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r \\ \begin{aligned} &=\int_{0}^{1}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\int_{0}^{1}\left({- 4 t - 9}\right)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\left[{- 2 t^{2} - 9 t}\right]_{0}^{1} \\ &=((-9)+(-2))-((0)+(0)) \\ &=(-11)-(0) \\ &=-11\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

$$

$$

$$

$$

question.:question/problem: Evaluate ${\int}_{C}F\cdot\text{d}r$ given that $F(x,y)=(- 2 x + 1)\,i+(- 2 y - 1)\,j$ and $C$ is the path $r(t)=(t \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i+(t \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j$ for $t\in[0,2 \pi].$
question.:question/worked-solution:
We will use the formula

$$
\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r=\int_a^b F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t.
$$

Along the curve $C,$ we have

$$
x=t \sin{\left(t \right)},\quad y=t \cos{\left(t \right)}.
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t)) \\ \begin{aligned} &=(- 2 x + 1)\,i+(- 2 y - 1)\,j \\ &=\begin{aligned}&\left(- 2 \left(t \sin{\left(t \right)}\right) + 1\right)\,i \\ &{} +\left(- 2 \left(t \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) - 1\right)\,j\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(- 2 t \sin{\left(t \right)} + 1)\,i \\ &{} +(- 2 t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 1)\,j\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{gathered}r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\ &=\begin{aligned}&\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i \\ &{} +\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i \\ &{} +(- t \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&\left({\begin{aligned}&(- 2 t \sin{\left(t \right)} + 1)\,i \\ &{} +(- 2 t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 1)\,j\end{aligned}}\right) \\ &{} \cdot\left({\begin{aligned}&(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i \\ &{} +(- t \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned}}\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(- 2 t \sin{\left(t \right)} + 1) \\ &{} \cdot(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)}) \\ &{} +(- 2 t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 1) \\ &{} \cdot(- t \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)})\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&\left({\begin{aligned}&- 2 t^{2} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)}  \\ &{} - 2 t \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)} + t \cos{\left(t \right)}  \\ &{} + \sin{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}}\right) \\ &{} +\left({\begin{aligned}&2 t^{2} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + t \sin{\left(t \right)}  \\ &{} - 2 t \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}}\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&t \sin{\left(t \right)} + t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2 t  \\ &{} + \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

Finally, we can evaluate the integral, as follows:

$$
\begin{gathered}\int_C F\cdot\text{d}r \\ \begin{aligned} &=\int_{0}^{2 \pi}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\int_{0}^{2 \pi}\left({\begin{aligned}&t \sin{\left(t \right)} + t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2 t  \\ &{} + \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}}\right)\,\text{d}t \\ &=\left[{- t^{2} + t \sin{\left(t \right)} - t \cos{\left(t \right)}}\right]_{0}^{2 \pi} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&((- 4 \pi^{2})+(0)+(- 2 \pi)) \\ &{} -((0)+(0)+(0))\end{aligned} \\ &=(- 4 \pi^{2} - 2 \pi)-(0) \\ &=- 2 \pi \left(1 + 2 \pi\right)\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

The offset terms integrate by the reverse product rule:

$$
\begin{gathered}\frac{\mathrm d}{\mathrm dt}\left(- t^{2} + t \sin{\left(t \right)} - t \cos{\left(t \right)}\right) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&t \sin{\left(t \right)} + t \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2 t  \\ &{} + \sin{\left(t \right)} - \cos{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}
$$

$$

Computing $r^{\prime}(t),$ we get

$$
\begin{gathered}r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\frac{\text{d}x}{\text{d}t}\,i+\frac{\text{d}y}{\text{d}t}\,j \\ &=\begin{aligned}&\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i \\ &{} +\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}t}(t \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i \\ &{} +(- t \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}

Therefore,

$$
\begin{gathered}F(r(t))\cdot r^{\prime}(t) \\ \begin{aligned} &=\begin{aligned}&\left({\begin{aligned}&(t \sin{\left(t \right)} + 1)\,i \\ &{} +(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + 2)\,j\end{aligned}}\right) \\ &{} \cdot\left({\begin{aligned}&(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)})\,i \\ &{} +(- t \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)})\,j\end{aligned}}\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&(t \sin{\left(t \right)} + 1) \\ &{} \cdot(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)}) \\ &{} +(t \cos{\left(t \right)} + 2) \\ &{} \cdot(- t \sin{\left(t \right)} + \cos{\left(t \right)})\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&\left({\begin{aligned}&t^{2} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} + t \sin^{2}{\left(t \right)}  \\ &{} + t \cos{\left(t \right)} + \sin{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}}\right) \\ &{} +\left({\begin{aligned}&- t^{2} \sin{\left(t \right)} \cos{\left(t \right)} - 2 t \sin{\left(t \right)}  \\ &{} + t \cos^{2}{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}}\right)\end{aligned} \\ &=\begin{aligned}&- 2 t \sin{\left(t \right)} + t \cos{\left(t \right)} + t  \\ &{} + \sin{\left(t \right)} + 2 \cos{\left(t \right)}\end{aligned}\end{aligned}\end{gathered}

$$
